subject: fennec
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module to model a fennec fox using the SDK, thinking through realistic proportions like its oversized ears, cream fur, and bushy black-tipped tail before writing the implementation.

Sketching out the skeleton structure now: hips, spine, neck, head, ears, tail, and four IK legs, plus the specific API calls I'll use like joint(), chain(), catmull curves, and sweep() for building geometry along those paths.

For materials, I'm planning the fur coloring using mottle and countershade to get a sandy-apricot back with a cream belly, dark tan ears outside with cream inner fur, and simple dark eye spheres with highlights.

Working out ear geometry now, using an extruded tall rounded-triangle outline angled outward and back to capture that distinctive fennec fox ear shape, then positioning them on the head in local coordinates.

Working out ear placement...

For the ear outline shape itself, I'm thinking of a rounded leaf-like profile with a low number of points for that low-poly look, using smoothing so the base is wide and the tip tapers into a soft rounded point rather than a sharp corner.

For the head I'm planning to use a swept profile along a short path from the cranium to the pointed snout, tapering the radius from wider at the skull to narrow at the nose tip, attached to the head bone, with a separate lower jaw sweep attached to its own jaw joint. I'm roughly blocking out body proportions in model space too -- chest-to-rump length around 0.4, shoulder height near 0.23, legs reaching down to the feet near ground level.

Now I'm working out the joint hierarchy: making hips the single root joint at the base of the spine, then building a spine chain parented to hips using a Catmull-Rom path through a few points rising up the back, naming the intermediate joints spine1 and spine2, and being careful that the chain's starting joint coincides with the hips position rather than duplicating a separate joint there.

For the neck and head, I'm chaining a 3-point path (base of neck, mid-neck, head) parented to the last spine joint, using the names array trick where giving one more name than spans (3 names for 2 spans) produces a tip joint -- so the chain itself can terminate in the head joint, aimed along the tangent direction, avoiding a separate head joint declaration.

I'm defining the jaw joint as a child of the head, positioned and aimed using head-local offsets (slightly forward and down) so it naturally sits below the head's pivot for mouth articulation.

Now I'm sketching the skull and snout geometry as a tapering sweep along head-local points, with radii narrowing from the skull toward the snout tip, then planning a similar thin tapered sweep for the jaw bone extending forward from the jaw joint.

For the eyes, I'm placing dark spheres on the skull sides using head-local coordinates offset left/right, forward, and up to position them appropriately relative to the snout and skull proportions.

Placing the eye sphere using azimuth/elevation around the head joint, with a null-hit check to skip if nothing's found. For the nose and ears, I'll use similar surface-hit logic centered on the snout tip and skull, picking different azimuth angles to position each feature outward from its local center.

Still writing placement logic...

For the inner ear piece, I'll scale the outer outline down (0.6 in y, 0.7 in x) and offset it slightly along the thickness so it sits centered on the front face in cream color.

Now I'm working out leg placement — front shoulder joints and foot targets positioned so the two-segment limb lengths (around 0.12 each) comfortably span the vertical distance, with a backward bend hint at the knee for a natural fennec stance.

For the hind legs, I'm setting the hip higher and farther back, using a three-segment digitigrade chain (thigh, shin, hock) with lengths summing to about 0.30 against a shorter vertical reach, requiring forward-knee and backward-hock bends to take up the slack. I'm working through how to name the chain joints so the path's four points correctly map to hip, knee, hock, and ankle/tip for the inverse kinematics solver.

For the front legs, I'm settling on a three-point chain (shoulder, elbow, wrist/paw) with two spans plus a tip joint, naming them with side suffixes like shoulderL/elbowL/wristL and hipL/kneeL/hockL/footL for the back, making sure all names are valid identifiers and that front legs parent to the first spine joint near the hips.

For feet, I'm adding small box geometry pads attached to the tip joints rather than spheres, positioned just above floor level. The legs themselves get swept geometry along the limb chains with a tapering radius from thick near the body to thinner at the foot, using rounded caps so the foot naturally touches the ground.

For the body, I'm sweeping a tube along the spine chain with a varying radius—narrower at hips, widest at mid-torso, slightly slimmer at chest—to match a fennec's slender build, checking that the resulting belly height clears the leg tops. For the coat, I'm layering a mottled sand-and-apricot base with cream countershading, plus darker tones for the nose, eyes, and tail tip, keeping the palette compact.

Now I'm designing the tail: a bushy, moderately long tail curling upward from the hips, built as a short chain of spine points with a radius profile that bulges in the middle for fluffiness and tapers toward a black tip, using color bands to switch from the body coat to the tip color near the end of the tail.

I'm also finishing up other coloring details -- dark eye liner and nose, cream inside the apricot-toned ears, a cream chest bib, dark brown eyes, and a pale fennec-style muzzle, while skipping whiskers and stripe patterns.

For the head, I'm using bands along the sweep path so the skull is coat-colored and the snout fades into cream near the tip, with the jaw also done in cream and a small dark nose sphere at the end. Now I'm setting up imports from the builder library and planning to use its countershade and mottle helpers for the overall coat pattern.

Defining color palette constants...

Writing the fennec build function, starting with the mottled sand-and-apricot coat countershaded toward cream, then constructing the hips joint and spine chain...

Still writing spine chain...

Building the neck chain and head joint, working through how joint indexing resolves the parent position along the catmull spline.

Now I'm sketching the skull sweep profile with points defined relative to the head joint's local frame, choosing back/forward/up offsets and radii to give the cranium a bulkier look fitting a fennec's large head.

For coloring, I'm setting the coat tone to dominate the earlier part of the head's path with cream taking over near the snout tip, using bands keyed off the sweep's t value.

Then I move to the jaw joint, parenting it to the head and aiming it forward and down to sit beneath the snout, planning its own small sweep profile positioned so the lower jaw tucks naturally under the head's forward point.

After that I work out the nose placement by sampling a point on the head surface near the snout tip and embedding a small sphere there for the nose, then do the same surface-sampling approach for the eyes, computing symmetric left/right hit points at an azimuth and elevation offset from the head's forward axis.

Now I'm defining the ear outline as a rounded trapezoid shape with points tracing out the ear's base, tip, and back curve, making sure the array is typed correctly as outline points for the sweep/extrude function.

For attaching ears, I'm finding hit points symmetrically on both sides of the skull surface at specific angles, then extruding the ear outline along that location with tapering thickness and a slight bevel for roundness. I realize the ear base needs to sink slightly below the surface rather than float on top, so I'm nudging the attachment point downward along the surface normal.

For the inner ear detail, I'm defining a smaller inner outline and extruding it onto the front face of the already-placed ear, making sure to explicitly specify the skeletal bone binding so both the outer and inner ear pieces correctly follow the head rather than defaulting to the wrong nearest joint.

Now I'm thinking through the body shape itself, planning a sweep along the spine chain with varying radii to form the torso, considering a separate neck sweep with its own tapering radii to blend into the body, and working out where the chest cap should sit at the end of the spine chain.

Then I'm defining the tail as a catmull-rom chain with three spans off the hips, with a sweep that varies radius from thin at the base to bushy mid-tail, tapering to a point, and adding a dark tip color band near the end.

Now I'm setting up the leg structure, looping over left and right sides to mirror positions, and starting to define the front shoulder and foot points for each leg.

Writing limb code...

Legs get a "leg" role, and I'm adding paw pads as small flat boxes at each foot's tip position so they sit touching the floor, using cream tones for the lower leg and paw to mimic a fennec's coloring. I need to handle the chain's tip joint carefully since it may be nullable, so I'll resolve it safely before placing the paw geometry.

For now I'll skip extras like whiskers, back stripes, and a chest bib to keep things simple, relying on existing dark ear backs and tail tip for detail. I'm double-checking that the sweep and bone parameters (head, tail, legs) are typed correctly so the geometry attaches properly to each joint.

I'm also verifying that unused imports like rng don't need to be included, confirming leg and chain point arrays are typed correctly for sweeps, and running ground-clearance checks on the paws, tail, and body so nothing sinks noticeably below the floor. Height-wise the fennec ends up a bit oversized with the ears factored in, but it's an acceptable stylized proportion. I'm finalizing hit-point placement for the ears and eyes, confirming typed tuples and outline point arrays, and then writing out the complete code with proper type annotations.
